plan.contextChunk: This figure pairs a coordinate diagram with a magnified inset to define the volume element in spherical coordinates. On the left, x, y, and z axes radiate from a common origin and a small curved orange box floats above the first octant, bounded by two dashed circular arcs of slightly different radii and by dashed rays fanning out from the origin. A bracket on the z axis marks the radial increment Delta rho, the angular gap between the two rays reaching the box is marked Delta phi, and a small angle in the horizontal plane near the origin is marked Delta theta. A flat blue quadrilateral in the xy-plane is the projection of the box, with a bracket beneath labeled rho sin phi and an arrow into it labeled rho sin phi Delta theta. A thick gray curved arrow sweeps right to an enlarged copy of the same box, whose three edges are labeled Delta rho, rho Delta phi, and rho sin phi Delta theta, with Delta V = rho^2 sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta printed below. Showing the subbox in place and again blown up lets each edge be matched to the coordinate increment that generates it. The construction motivates the factor rho^2 sin phi that appears when a triple integral is rewritten in spherical coordinates.

interactions.teaches: The radial thickness of the spherical subbox contributes one linear factor, Delta rho, to the volume element

interactions.label: Delta phi
interactions.teaches: A change in polar angle becomes a physical arc length rho Delta phi, so the angular increment is multiplied by the radius

interactions.label: Delta theta

demo_steps.title: The default spherical element
demo_steps.narration: The orange element sits between two nearby radii, two nearby polar angles, and two nearby azimuthal angles. Its magnified copy labels the three edge lengths that multiply to approximate the small volume.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the radial thickness
demo_steps.narration: Increasing Delta rho thickens the element outward from the origin. Only the radial edge changes, matching the factor Delta rho in the volume formula.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the polar arc
demo_steps.narration: Increasing Delta phi opens the element in the vertical meridian. The physical edge is not Delta phi itself but the arc length rho Delta phi.

demo_steps.title: Stretch the azimuthal arc
demo_steps.narration: Increasing Delta theta widens the blue footprint around the horizontal circle. The corresponding edge length is rho sin phi Delta theta, using the projected radius rho sin phi.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Use an axonometric/isometric-style view matching the source: z appears vertical upward, y points to the right, and x points diagonally down-left. Overall coordinate diagram should occupy the left 60% of the frame; enlarged inset sits on the right 35%, slightly above center, with the formula below it. World-space axes: x, y, z each span about 3.5 units from the origin; draw arrowheads at positive ends only. Use mathematical spherical coordinates x = rho sin(phi) cos(theta), y = rho sin(phi) sin(theta), z = rho cos(phi), with phi measured down from +z and theta measured in the xy-plane. Fix the inner radius rho0 = 2.15 units, central polar angle phi0 = 0.90 rad, and central azimuth theta0 = 0.62 rad; the sliders set increments Delta rho, Delta phi, and Delta theta from those lower bounds. The in-place orange element is the curved cell over rho in [rho0, rho0 + Delta rho], phi in [phi0, phi0 + Delta phi], theta in [theta0, theta0 + Delta theta]. Sample each curved face with at least a 6 by 6 grid so the spherical curvature is visible but still textbook-simple. Default edge lengths at the mid-radius should be Delta rho = 0.35, rho Delta phi about 0.54, and rho sin(phi) Delta theta about 0.47. The blue projection is the footprint of the same rho-theta bounds at z = 0, using projected radius r = rho sin(phi); keep it flat on the xy-plane under the orange element. The enlarged inset is a separate scaled copy, not physically connected: place it to the right, about 4.6 world units from the origin and 1.4 units above the xy-plane in screen composition. Its three local dimensions should be proportional to Delta rho, rho_mid Delta phi, and rho_mid sin(phi_mid) Delta theta, scaled by about 2.3 relative to the in-place element; orient it with its longest visible face slanting up-right like the source. Color palette: axes and text black #000000; dashed construction arcs medium gray #555555; gray sweep arrow #b8b8b8 with darker outline #999999; orange faces translucent #f7944d at 35% opacity; orange outlines #f05a24; blue projection #3b6fb6 at 45% opacity with dark blue outline #173f7a. Edge highlights should use distinct saturated colors: Delta rho red-orange #e53935, rho Delta phi purple #7b1fa2, rho sin phi Delta theta blue #1565c0. Volume formula must read exactly: Delta V = rho^2 sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta, using Greek symbols in the rendered labels if supported.
interactionPlan.notes: Implement the spherical cell as six parametric surface patches: rho-min, rho-max, phi-min, phi-max, theta-min, and theta-max, with transparent orange material and depth-sorted rendering. Use LineSegments or dashed line materials for construction rays and arcs. The inset may be rendered as a local affine approximation of the spherical cell with slightly curved top/front edges, keeping labels easier to read. When a slider is being dragged, highlight the corresponding edge on both the in-place element and the enlarged inset. The labelOverlay toggle should hide one label set and show the other without moving the geometry. Keep text as screen-facing sprites or CSS2D labels so the figure remains readable during orbit.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for Delta rho, Delta phi, and Delta theta: the learner drags each increment and the orange spherical subbox plus its magnified inset stretch along the matching edge, making clear how the three coordinate increments multiply into Delta V.
- Toggle between in-place and enlarged element labels: the learner switches label overlays on the coordinate diagram and the inset, and the same edge is highlighted in both locations, making clear why rho Delta phi and rho sin phi Delta theta are arc-length factors rather than raw angle measures.

authoredContext:
Now we can illustrate the following theorem for triple integrals in spherical coordinates with (ρijk*,θijk*,φijk*) being any sample point in the spherical subbox Bijk. For the volume element of the subbox ΔV in spherical coordinates, we have ΔV=(Δρ)(ρΔφ)(ρsinφΔθ),, as shown in the following figure.

The volume element of a box in spherical coordinates.

In the spherical coordinate space, a box is projected onto the polar coordinate plane. On the polar coordinate plane, the projection has area rho sin phi Delta theta. On the z axis, a distance Delta rho is indicated, and from these boundaries, angles are made that project through the edges of the box. There is also a blown up version of the box that shows it has sides Delta rho, rho Delta phi, and rho sin phi Delta theta, with overall volume Delta V = rho squared sin phi Delta rho Delta phi Delta theta.

As with the other multiple integrals we have examined, all the properties work similarly for a triple integral in the spherical coordinate system, and so do the iterated integrals. Fubini’s theorem takes the following form.

discrepancies: The default view hides the coordinate-diagram labels such as Δφ, Δθ, Δρ, and ρ sin φ even though the source shows them together with the enlarged-element labels.
The enlarged orange element appears almost front-on and rectangular, rather than a skewed parallelepiped with clearly visible slanted top and side faces as in the source.
The main spherical wedge and its dashed construction arcs are compressed near the vertical axis; the source shows a broader, more oblique spherical sector extending to the right of the z-axis.
The y-axis and its label are not prominent in the rendered view, while the source has a clear y-axis extending to the right.
The generated figure uses thick red, purple, and blue highlighted edges, whereas the source mainly uses orange element edges with black annotation arrows.
evaluation.notes: The spherical volume-element concept is accurate and interactive, but the default composition, label visibility, inset shape, and color emphasis differ noticeably from the source.
action_items: Show both coordinate-diagram and enlarged-element labels by default, matching the source figure rather than hiding one group behind the overlay selector.
Reorient and enlarge the main spherical wedge so it sits more clearly to the right of the z-axis with broader dashed meridian arcs.
Adjust the enlarged inset to look like the skewed parallelepiped in the source with three visible faces and a stronger slant.
Tone down the colored edge highlights or replace them with orange edges and black leader arrows closer to the original annotation style.

feedback.rationale: The concept and interactivity are strong, but the remaining issues are implementation-level fixes involving default label visibility, geometry orientation, inset shape, and color styling.
